items.text: Coherent Corp. warns that limitations on intellectual-property protection, third-party infringement claims, litigation, indemnification obligations, legal proceedings, regulatory investigations, inquiries, and other claims could materially adversely affect its business, results of operations, or financial condition. Its U.S. government research and development contracts may require project-specific technology to be disclosed to competitors through contract reporting, and some development projects may assign resulting intellectual property to the other party or make it jointly owned without Coherent retaining exclusive rights, potentially weakening its competitive position. Successful infringement claims could require Coherent to pay substantial damages or royalties, obtain licenses, or modify products or processes. As of the August 14, 2026 filing, Coherent and its subsidiaries were involved in claims and lawsuits incidental to their business; management, after consulting legal counsel, believed ultimate liabilities would not materially affect financial condition, liquidity, or results of operations, although unfavorable resolutions remained possible.

Coherent Corp. warns that execution failures in streamlining its product portfolio, exiting business segments, restructuring, implementing its acquisitions strategy, integrating acquired companies, product lines, businesses, assets, and personnel, or capitalizing on strategic divestitures could impair operations, demand support, market share, and anticipated strategic, cost-saving, or financial benefits. Integration may be more difficult, costly, and time-consuming than anticipated, including because of risks to key employees and existing customers. Coherent expects to continue considering complementary acquisitions and expanding through additional acquisitions, but warns that transactions may require significant management time and financial resources, use available cash, issue dilutive equity, incur significant debt, assume contingent liabilities, create goodwill or intangible-asset impairment charges, or face antitrust and other regulatory action; competition, industry consolidation, high valuations, and integration difficulties may also prevent suitable transactions or sufficient scale and technological advantages.
For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported interest expense of $190,267 ($000), other income, net of $(140,139) ($000), and a $124,133 ($000) gain on sale of business.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. had no borrowings outstanding under its Revolving Credit Facility, $664 million of undrawn capacity, and compliance with all covenants under the Senior Credit Facilities; the company reported comparable available borrowing capacity of $315 million as of June 30, 2025.

Coherent Corp. recognized a $124,133 ($000) gain on the sale of businesses during the year ended June 30, 2026, including a $115 million gain from the September 2, 2025 sale of its aerospace and defense business for approximately $400 million; the aerospace and defense transaction also generated approximately $9 million of transaction-related costs in fiscal 2026.

Coherent Corp. has experienced cybersecurity incidents, including some data breaches, none of which had been determined to be material as of August 14, 2026. The company expects additional cyber-attacks and security incidents; evolving cybersecurity, data-privacy, and AI laws, standards, and market expectations may also require additional direct compliance costs, while customers, suppliers, or partners may be reluctant to share information or solutions because of actual or perceived inadequate controls. Incidents or compliance failures affecting Coherent Corp. or third-party providers could disrupt operations, cause damages, claims, expenses, reputational or competitive harm, impair insurance coverage, result in regulatory actions or liabilities, and materially adversely affect the business, results of operations, or financial condition.

Coherent's Industrial segment supplies excimer, solid-state, and CO2 lasers; high-power laser systems and subsystems; engineered materials; laser optics; thermoelectric components; and advanced ceramic and metal-matrix composite products for semiconductor capital equipment, display manufacturing, precision manufacturing, scientific research, life sciences, and scientific instrumentation. Coherent's metal-matrix composites and reaction-bonded ceramics address semiconductor capital equipment requirements for tighter tolerances, enhanced thermal stability, faster wafer transfer speeds, and reduced stage settling times through their light weight, strength, hardness, and coefficient of thermal expansion.

Effective July 1, 2025, Coherent Corp. realigned its organizational structure and aggregated its operating segments into two reportable segments, Datacenter & Communications and Industrial, under ASC 280 based on similarities in economic characteristics, products and services, production processes, customer types, and distribution methods. Comparative prior-period segment information was recast to conform; consolidated results, financial condition, and cash flows were not affected. Coherent reported through these two segments for fiscal 2026.

Coherent Corp. expanded and invested in its Sherman, Texas, manufacturing capacity during fiscal 2026, including indium phosphide capacity, in response to increased customer demand and an industry-wide shortage; Coherent also states that it is expanding global 6-inch InP manufacturing capacity in the United States and Europe and operates multiple 6-inch GaAs VCSEL manufacturing facilities to support increasing customer demand. InP is described as a foundational technology for next-generation AI optical interconnects. Coherent warns that capacity expansions and capital expenditures may not be completed on schedule, may require higher costs, may fail to generate expected returns or cash flows, or may be underutilized if demand is insufficient. If demand exceeds its organic capabilities and Coherent cannot identify or execute a strategic acquisition, it may be unable to address demand.

Coherent Corp. recorded preferred stock dividends of $31,751 ($000) for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared with $123,688 ($000) for the year ended June 30, 2025; preferred stock deemed dividends were $3,351 ($000) and $6,238 ($000), respectively. The amounts reflect obligations before and after the Series B conversion.
For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported research and development expense of $722,952 ($000).

For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported $64 million of additional non-cash impairment charges in its Industrial segment related to three entities, reducing their carrying values to estimated fair value; the financial statements reported impairment of assets held-for-sale of $64,404 ($000). Two entities had been classified as held-for-sale since the prior fiscal year-end and a third was classified as held-for-sale during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.

On December 4, 2023, Silicon Carbide LLC, a Coherent Corp. subsidiary, received an aggregate $1 billion in cash from Denso Corporation and Mitsubishi Electric Corporation in exchange for 25% of Silicon Carbide LLC's equity. Denso purchased 16,666,667 Class A Common Units for $500,000,000, and Mitsubishi Electric Corporation purchased 16,666,667 Class A Common Units for $500,000,000. The investment was and is intended primarily to fund future capital expansion of the silicon carbide business and increase Coherent Corp.'s available free cash flow and financial and operational flexibility.

On September 2, 2025, Coherent Corp. completed the sale of its aerospace and defense business, part of the Industrial segment, for approximately $400 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. The sale generated a $115 million gain and approximately $9 million of transaction-related costs in fiscal 2026.

During the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. received $1,250,000 ($000) under the Term A Facility, $3,267 ($000) under the Term B Facility, and $640,075 ($000) from revolving credit facilities; it also issued common shares for $1,998,552 ($000), repaid $1,723,437 ($000) of existing debt, repaid $676,211 ($000) of revolving-credit borrowings, and made $509 million of payments on its Term Facilities, including $502 million of voluntary payments.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp.'s SG&A expense was $1,044,566 ($000), or approximately $1,045 million and 15% of revenues, compared with $926 million, or 16% of revenues, in the prior year. The increase was primarily driven by higher legal, integration and divestiture-related consulting costs, facility exit costs, and share-based and variable compensation expense, partly offset by cost-reduction efficiencies.

Coherent Corp. warns that global or regional economic downturns, including those caused by inflation, geopolitics, major central-bank policy actions such as interest-rate increases, or public-health crises, could reduce short-term and long-term customer demand, create industry oversupply, increase customer inventory levels, weaken credit markets, and lower product pricing, adversely affecting its business, results of operations, and financial condition.

Coherent Corp. reported research and development expenditures of $723 million, $582 million, and $479 million for fiscal years 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively; the fiscal 2026 financial statements reported the more precise fiscal 2026 R&D expense as $722.952 million. For fiscal 2025, R&D expenses were $582 million, or 10% of revenues, versus $479 million, or 10% of revenues, for fiscal 2024; the $103 million increase primarily reflected continued investment in product portfolios, particularly datacom, focused on projects with the highest return on investment.

Coherent Corp. recorded $85 million of non-cash impairment charges on assets held for sale in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 and $64 million in fiscal 2026. The fiscal 2025 charges reduced the carrying values of entities held for sale to estimated fair value, and management had entered into non-binding agreements to sell the entities. Fiscal 2026 also included a $124 million gain on the sale of businesses. Separately, Coherent stated that the January 30, 2026 sale of its Munich product division involved a $96 million loss, impairment charges of $81 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, $13 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, and $11 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, partially offset by a $9 million gain on sale of business in fiscal 2026.

During the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. sold 7,788 common shares and received $1,998,450 ($000) net of $1,575 ($000) in issuance costs; common-share issuance proceeds were approximately $1,999 million in fiscal 2026, compared with $— in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024.
Coherent Corp.'s optical networking solutions are designed for AI networking and communications applications with low power consumption, compact form factors, and efficient deployment.

Coherent Corp. has a substantial and diversified global manufacturing footprint, internal production capabilities for many critical components, and a global supply chain that provide flexibility in sourcing and manufacturing and help support customer demand and business continuity. Coherent states that these capabilities are intended to mitigate tariffs, trade sanctions, and other geopolitical challenges, while its reliance on third-party suppliers, contract manufacturers, specialized equipment, strategic materials, integrated circuits, mechanical housings, and optical components remains a production and continuity constraint.

Before its conversion in the quarter ended December 31, 2025, Coherent Corp.'s Series B Preferred Stock initially carried voting rights with Common Stock on an as-converted basis, subject to limited exceptions. It was initially measured at fair value less issuance costs and accreted to redemption value over 10 years using the effective interest method; the accretion was recorded as deemed dividends reducing net earnings (loss) available to common shareholders.

Coherent Corp. reported that during the year ended June 30, 2026, 30,122 shares of Series A preferred stock were converted, eliminating 2,506,885 ($000) of recorded Series A preferred-stock balance and 215 noncontrolling-interest shares. Coherent also reported a conversion of 2,300 Series A preferred shares into 10,240 common shares that removed $445,319 ($000) of preferred-stock amount; the reported figures are retained as stated and are not reconciled here.
Coherent Corp. reported $436,992 ($000) of net proceeds from the sale of a business and $89,384 ($000) from the sale of an equity investment during the year ended June 30, 2026.

Coherent Corp.'s net cash provided by financing activities was $1,477 million for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared with net cash used of $452 million for the year ended June 30, 2025 and net cash provided of $758 million for the year ended June 30, 2024. Fiscal 2026 financing included approximately $2 billion in net proceeds from issuing common stock to NVIDIA, $1,921 million received from long-term borrowings and revolving credit facilities, $676 million paid on revolving-credit borrowings, and $1,723 million paid on existing debt.

Coherent Corp.’s interest and other, net expense was $244 million in fiscal 2024, $196 million in fiscal 2025, and $50 million for the year ended June 30, 2026. Term Facilities interest expense was $139 million in the year ended June 30, 2026 and $192 million in the year ended June 30, 2025. The interest rate cap and interest rate swap reduced interest expense by $17 million in fiscal 2026 and $32 million in fiscal 2025, respectively, while amortization of debt issuance costs was $17 million in both years. The fiscal 2026 decrease in interest and other, net expense primarily reflected a $74 million gain on the sale of an equity investment, $53 million lower interest expense, and $34 million lower foreign-exchange net losses.

Coherent Corp.'s effective income tax rate was 68% for fiscal 2025, compared with (8)% for fiscal 2024, and 7% for fiscal 2026, compared with 68% for fiscal 2025. Coherent stated that fiscal 2025 was affected by the classification of assets held for sale and an increase in the U.S. valuation allowance, while the fiscal 2026 variance from the 21% U.S. statutory federal income tax rate was primarily driven by releases of uncertain tax positions, excess tax benefits from stock-based compensation, benefits from changes in German tax law, and differences between U.S. and foreign tax rates. Foreign tax holidays reduced the effective tax rate by 0.9%, 11.6%, and 5.6% and increased diluted earnings per share by $0.04, $0.06, and $0.05 for fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.

Coherent Corp.'s Board approved the 2023 Plan in May 2023, covering site consolidations, facility moves and closures, and the relocation and requalification of certain manufacturing facilities. Beginning in the quarter ended March 31, 2025, management approved the 2025 Plan as part of its ongoing strategic review. The 2025 Plan covers severance and benefits, lease and contract termination costs, asset write-offs, facilities moves, workforce reductions, and other restructuring costs; the two plans are collectively called the Restructuring Plans. Coherent expects the 2025 Plan restructuring actions to be substantially completed by the end of fiscal 2026, but stated on August 14, 2026 that actual timing and costs may differ materially from current expectations and estimates.

Coherent Corp. reported approximately $370 million of pre-tax restructuring charges during fiscal years 2023 to 2026, primarily for workforce reductions and facility consolidations related to site closures and relocations. It reported restructuring charges of $160 million in fiscal 2025 and $63 million in fiscal 2026. Separately, the 2025 Plan generated $107 million of net charges in the year ended June 30, 2025 and $62 million in the year ended June 30, 2026, primarily for property and equipment write-offs, employee termination costs, and site-closure costs. The 2023 Restructuring Plan generated net charges of $27 million in fiscal 2024, $53 million in the year ended June 30, 2025, and $1 million in the year ended June 30, 2026, primarily for site move costs, partly offset by adjustments to employee termination costs. The disclosures report different charge measures and are retained separately rather than reconciled. The fiscal 2026 disclosure also reported $64 million of impairment charges on assets held for sale and a $124 million gain on sale of business, while fiscal 2025 included $85 million of such impairment charges.

Coherent Corp. issued 75,000 Series B-1 Preferred Stock shares in March 2021 for $10,000 per share, an aggregate purchase price of $750 million, and issued 140,000 Series B-2 Preferred Stock shares on July 1, 2022 for $10,000 per share, an aggregate purchase price of $1.4 billion. All outstanding Series B-1 and Series B-2 Convertible Preferred Stock was converted into Common Stock during the quarter ended December 31, 2025; the 75,000 Series B-1 shares and 140,000 Series B-2 shares were converted into an aggregate of 30.1 million Common Stock shares. During the year ended June 30, 2026, $2.5 billion was reclassified from Mezzanine Equity to Common Stock, and no Series B Preferred Stock remained issued and outstanding thereafter.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp.'s R&D expense increased to $723 million, or 10% of revenues, from $582 million, or 10% of revenues. Coherent stated that the increased investment focused particularly on its Datacenter & Communications portfolio, including 800G/1.6T transceivers, co-packaged optics, optical circuit switches, multi-rail solutions, VCSELs, EMLs, silicon photonics, ICs, isolators, thermoelectric coolers, 400G/lane components supporting 3.2T and 6.4T, coherent transceivers, and next-generation pump lasers, to support near- and long-term revenue growth and new high-margin, high-value systems.

Coherent Corp. offers CW lasers, advanced ultrafast-pulsed laser sources, and high-energy pulsed excimer gas lasers for microscopy, neuroscience, and optogenetics, selling these systems globally to universities and research institutions.

Coherent Corp. has technical expertise and manufacturing capabilities spanning specialty-materials growth and fabrication, semiconductor and high-power lasers, passive optics including isolators, transceivers, transport equipment, internally developed custom integrated software, strategic components, crystals, fibers, and laser-based systems. Coherent identifies vertical integration, manufacturing facilities and equipment, experienced technical and manufacturing employees, product quality, on-time delivery, ability to scale, intellectual property, and worldwide marketing and distribution channels as competitive advantages. Its success in developing and manufacturing products depends on tailoring the optical and physical properties of technically challenging materials, components, and photonics-based solutions while controlling quality and in-process yields; Coherent states that this expertise supports delivering volume solutions at scale. It relies on its own production and design capability for certain strategic components and uses rare-earth materials in some production processes. In life sciences, Coherent vertically integrates materials such as medical-use crystals and ZnS materials for NIR and IR spectroscopy through high-precision components, complex subassemblies, and full subsystems.

Coherent Corp. warns that products and technologies failing to meet target specifications, containing actual or perceived defects, producing inadequate yields, or being incompatible with end uses could impose significant costs and create product-quality and product-liability risks. Coherent has experienced problems with nonconforming, defective, or incompatible products after shipment, and customers may discover defects only after products are fully deployed and operated under peak stress conditions. Failure to correct such defects or other problems could result in customer loss, increased product-return and warranty costs, brand-reputation damage, failure to attract new customers or achieve market acceptance, diversion of development and engineering resources, or customer legal action. Coherent may also incur compensation, replacement, warranty, recall, product-liability, or other costs, with liability potentially increasing when products perform critical functions or are deemed responsible for functionality in customers' products. The company also cannot be sure of end-market pricing, specifications, yield, or customer acceptance.

Coherent Corp.'s international operations and manufacturing facilities are subject to complex and rapidly changing domestic and international laws, regulations, and industry standards covering anti-corruption, anti-money-laundering, anticompetition, import/export, environmental, health and safety, product, cybersecurity, data privacy, AI, and facility operations. Coherent stated on August 14, 2026 that noncompliance by the company, its employees, contractors, suppliers, or agents, or changes in these requirements could limit sales, product development, manufacturing, and shipments; increase procurement, remediation, and compliance costs; require process changes; cause regulatory penalties, fines, civil or criminal sanctions, legal liabilities, reputational damage, or adverse financial results; and materially adversely affect its business, results of operations, or financial condition.

Coherent Corp. warns that adverse foreign-currency movements may negatively affect revenue, cost of sales, operating margins, and foreign-exchange losses; as of June 30, 2026, its primary currency exposures were the Chinese Renminbi, Euro, Swiss Franc, Japanese Yen, Singapore Dollar, and Korean Won. Because subsidiaries transact or hold assets and liabilities in currencies different from their functional currencies, exchange-rate volatility may increase foreign customers' local-currency product prices or manufacturing costs and adversely affect financial condition, cash flows, and profitability; foreign-exchange controls may also prevent repatriation of cash held outside the United States.

Coherent's Datacenter & Communications segment supplies transceivers, co-packaged optics, optical circuit switches, modules, subsystems, semiconductor devices, optical amplifiers, passive optical components, optical line systems, transport products, coherent transmission components and transceivers, and a multi-rail platform for datacenter and communications applications, including VCSELs, EELs, pump lasers, optics, and ICs. Coherent describes itself as a leading supplier of optical transceivers for AI datacenter and networking applications, with a protocol-agnostic portfolio supporting Ethernet, InfiniBand, NVIDIA NVLink, and other AI networking architectures; its optical portfolio supports AI datacenter architectures, datacenter connectivity, and distributed-datacenter interconnect applications. Coherent stated that strong demand continued in its Datacenter and Communications markets, with hyperscale and other cloud-provider investment in AI datacenter infrastructure significantly boosting demand for datacenter transceivers. Demand was driven by AI growth, the transition from copper to optical connectivity, and rising bandwidth and energy-efficiency requirements in complex datacenter architectures.

At June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. held $825 million of time deposits with maturities of one year or less in short-term investments; they were classified as Level 1 and approximated fair value because of their short-term maturities.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. had tax credit carryforwards of $102.973 million in federal research and development credits expiring from June 2037 through June 2045, $13.224 million in foreign tax credits expiring from June 2030 through June 2036, $13.354 million in state tax credits expiring from June 2026 through June 2040, and $82.435 million in state tax credits with indefinite expiration. It also had operating-loss carryforwards of $26.712 million in federal losses expiring from June 2027 through June 2036, $1.539 million in federal losses with indefinite expiration, and $350.496 million in state losses expiring from June 2027 through June 2046. Coherent had recorded valuation allowances against the majority of its foreign and state loss and credit carryforwards, certain U.S. credit carryforwards, and the majority of state credit carryforwards; its U.S. federal loss carryforwards, federal research and development credit carryforwards, foreign tax credits, and certain acquisition-related state tax credits were subject to annual limitations under Section 382 of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code, which may restrict utilization of these tax attributes.
For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported cost of goods sold of $4,449.141 million.

Coherent Corp.’s credit agreement, originally dated July 1, 2022, provided $4.0 billion of senior secured financing: an $850 million Term A Facility maturing July 1, 2027; a $2,800 million Term B Facility maturing July 1, 2029; and a $350 million Revolving Credit Facility maturing July 1, 2027, including a letter-of-credit sub-facility of up to $50 million. Amendment No. 1 dated March 31, 2023 replaced the adjusted LIBOR-based interest rate with an adjusted SOFR-based rate. Amendment No. 2 dated April 2, 2024 replaced the outstanding Existing Term B Loans with an equal amount of New Term B Loans, without changing principal, while modifying the applicable interest rate and certain other provisions. Amendment No. 3 dated January 2, 2025 replaced the outstanding New Term B Loans with an equal amount of New Term B-2 Loans having substantially similar terms, except for the applicable interest rate and certain other provisions, while leaving the maturity of the New Term B-2 Loans and Revolving Credit Facility unchanged. On September 26, 2025, Coherent Corp. refinanced its existing revolving credit commitments, added $350 million of senior secured incremental revolving commitments, increased total revolving commitments to $700 million including a letter-of-credit sub-facility of up to $100 million, and added $1,250 million of senior secured incremental Term A loans; proceeds were used in part to repay all outstanding principal, interest and fees of the Existing Term A Loans. As of June 30, 2026, the 2025 Revolving Loans and 2025 Incremental Term A Loans bore interest at an adjusted SOFR rate subject to a 0.00% floor plus 1.50% and matured on the earlier of September 26, 2030 or an applicable Springing Maturity Date.

Coherent Corp.'s Datacenter & Communications segment profit was $1,329.719 million in fiscal 2026, compared with $903.787 million in fiscal 2025 and $499.968 million in fiscal 2024. Fiscal 2026 revenue increased by $1,519 million, or 40%, primarily because of continued strong AI datacenter demand, especially for transceivers, and higher Communications volumes from datacenter interconnect, scale-across, and traditional telecom applications; segment profit growth was partly offset by increased R&D investment.

Coherent Corp.'s international manufacturing, sourcing, and foreign-customer revenue expose it to tariffs, retaliatory measures, geopolitical tensions, export restrictions, restrictions on rare earth minerals, and other trade barriers. Coherent stated in its August 14, 2026 10-K that U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security restrictions on sales of certain EAR-controlled products to Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd. and certain affiliates without a BIS-issued license, as well as possible retaliatory actions by foreign governments amid trade tensions with China, could limit or prevent business with certain customers or suppliers, impose product-supply conditions, require licensing or intellectual-property transfers, increase costs, reduce demand, disrupt operations, and materially adversely affect its business, results of operations, or financial condition.

On March 2, 2026, Coherent Corp. entered into a multi-year, non-exclusive strategic agreement with NVIDIA covering advanced optics development, manufacturing capacity, and research and development, including a multi-billion-dollar purchase commitment and future access and capacity rights for advanced laser and optical networking products supporting next-generation AI infrastructure. NVIDIA invested $2 billion by purchasing 7,788,161 Coherent common shares at $256.80 per share in a private placement; the shares are subject to a six-month contractual lock-up and six-month price protection classified as equity. Coherent plans to use the proceeds for research and development, future capacity, operations, and manufacturing-capability expansion, which may require incremental equipment, labor, and working capital through 2030.

Tax holidays for certain business lines of Coherent Malaysia Sdn. Bhd., II-VI Laser Enterprise Philippines, Inc., Silicon Carbide Vietnam Limited Liability Company, Coherent Vietnam (Dong Nai) Company Limited, and Coherent Singapore Pte. Ltd. expired during the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. Remaining specified holidays expire in December 2027, on July 31, 2028, or on June 30, 2030; the Vietnam entities retain 50% tax holidays through June 30, 2030. The expirations may increase Coherent Corp.'s future tax burden.

During fiscal 2026, Coherent Corp.'s performance share unit activity included 2,138,134 nonvested units at June 30, 2025, 624,116 units granted at a weighted average grant-date fair value of $148.94, 315,066 units vested at $58.08, 72,581 units forfeited at $88.17, and 23,282 units resulting from performance adjustments at $58.08.

Before conversion in the quarter ended December 31, 2025, each Series B Preferred Stock share of Coherent Corp. was convertible at the holder's election into Common Stock at a conversion price of $85 per share, subject to adjustment; Coherent could force conversion if its Common Stock volume-weighted average price exceeded 150% of the applicable conversion price for 20 trading days in any 30-consecutive-trading-day period.

Coherent Corp. stated that employees hired after January 1, 2007 are ineligible for its U.S. qualified and nonqualified pension plans, employees hired after 2000 are ineligible for its primary German pension plan, and future compensation benefit accruals under both U.S. plans have been frozen since August 31, 2018.

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Coherent Corp. completed its annual impairment test of the indefinite-lived Coherent trade name, which had a carrying value of $430 million, and concluded that it was not impaired; the quantitative relief-from-royalty test as of April 1, 2026 found fair value well in excess of carrying value.

For financial reporting, Coherent Corp. depreciates buildings, building improvements, and land improvements primarily over 10 to 30 years, and machinery and equipment over 3 to 20 years, using the straight-line method.
Coherent Corp. recorded a $73,998 ($000) gain on the sale of an equity investment during the year ended June 30, 2026.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. had approximately $11.8 billion of estimated vendor purchase commitments and approximately $375 million of operating lease obligations, including $78 million payable in fiscal year 2027.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported cash and cash equivalents of $1,162 million, restricted cash of $606 million, consisting of $35 million classified as current and $571 million as non-current, and total cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $1,768,396 ($000), compared with cash and cash equivalents of $909 million, restricted cash of $9 million, and total cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $1,632,913 ($000) as of June 30, 2025; short-term investments were $825 million and $715 million, respectively.

At June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported $606 million of total restricted cash, including $604 million held by Silicon Carbide LLC and restricted for use only by that subsidiary; at June 30, 2025, total restricted cash was $724 million, including $720 million held by Silicon Carbide LLC. The Silicon Carbide LLC balances were unavailable for general corporate use.

Coherent Corp.'s development and manufacturing operations use or generate hazardous materials and require facilities, equipment, chemicals, and materials subject to extensive environmental, health, safety, product, cybersecurity, data privacy, AI, and facility-operation requirements. Coherent stated on August 14, 2026 that noncompliance or regulatory changes could require substantial capital and other expenditures, remediation, altered manufacturing processes, increased compliance costs, or procedures; suspend production or product sales; limit supplies of chemicals or materials; and result in third-party claims, regulatory scrutiny, fines, cleanup liabilities, civil or criminal sanctions, legal liabilities, reputational damage, and adverse effects on liquidity, results of operations, or financial condition.

Coherent Corp. entered into an interest-rate cap on February 23, 2022, amended it on March 20, 2023, made it effective July 1, 2023, and increased its notional amount from $500 million to $1,500 million on September 1, 2024. The cap gives Coherent the right to receive payment when one-month SOFR exceeds 1.92%, at a fixed monthly premium based on an annual rate of 0.853%, and hedges variable-rate borrowings. Coherent designated the cap as a cash-flow hedge for variability in SOFR-based interest payments on the Term Facilities; changes in fair value are initially recorded in AOCI and reclassified into interest expense over the corresponding periods. The cap is a Level 2 item, with fair value of $3 million at June 30, 2026, compared with $17 million at June 30, 2025.

Pillar Two had no material impact on Coherent Corp.'s Consolidated Financial Statements in fiscal years 2026, 2025, or 2024, according to Coherent Corp.; the company warned that further implementation changes to the OECD's 15% global minimum tax could have a material impact in future reporting periods. On January 5, 2026, the OECD announced a Pillar Two safe-harbour package including a potentially applicable “side-by-side” elective safe harbour for U.S.-parented multinational entities such as Coherent for fiscal years beginning after January 1, 2026; the package does not affect domestic taxation of foreign subsidiaries, and Coherent stated that related changes could affect its effective tax rate and cash tax payments.

Coherent Corp. reported net loss attributable to noncontrolling interests of $18 million for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared with $19 million for fiscal 2025 and $3 million for fiscal 2024; these amounts represented the noncontrolling interest holders' shares of Silicon Carbide LLC losses.

Coherent Corp. identifies operating activities, long-term borrowings, advance funding from customers, equity issuance, stock-option exercises, and sales of equity investments and businesses as historical cash sources; net cash provided by operating activities was $80 million in fiscal 2026, $634 million in fiscal 2025, and $546 million in fiscal 2024, while proceeds from common-share issuance were $1,999 million in fiscal 2026 and $— in fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024.

Coherent Corp. reported net earnings attributable to Coherent Corp. of $49 million for the year ended June 30, 2025, compared with a net loss of $156 million for fiscal 2024. A separate Coherent disclosure reported net earnings of $30,057 ($000) for fiscal 2025 and $786,884 ($000) for fiscal 2026, with net earnings available to common shareholders of $769,896 ($000) in fiscal 2026; the disclosures are contradictory and both figures are retained.

Coherent Corp.'s net cash provided by operating activities fell to $80 million for the year ended June 30, 2026, from $634 million in fiscal 2025 and $546 million in fiscal 2024; fiscal 2026 working-capital changes included cash reductions of $(367,631) ($000) from accounts receivable, $(1,183,000) ($000) from inventories, and $(9,307) ($000) from contract liabilities, partly offset by a $748,533 ($000) increase from accounts payable, while higher net earnings also partly offset the decrease.

Coherent Corp. periodically engages consultants, auditors, and other third parties to design, implement, assess, monitor, and test cybersecurity policies, procedures, and safeguards, and works with third-party suppliers and service providers on appropriate security measures.

Coherent Corp.'s Chief Information Officer and Global Head of Cybersecurity oversee the company's cybersecurity policies and processes, including prevention, detection, mitigation, and remediation. As disclosed in the 10-K filed August 14, 2026, they have combined relevant experience of more than 45 years, including over 20 years in cybersecurity, and Coherent devotes significant resources and assigns these high-level personnel to cybersecurity risk mitigation and addressing safeguard gaps.

As of August 14, 2026, Coherent Corp. was increasingly incorporating artificial-intelligence capabilities into technology development, business operations, products, and services. The company stated that implementation may be costly and may not improve operations or produce products and services preferred by customers, and identified broader uncertainty and potential adverse impacts associated with the use and evolution of AI. AI-related execution, competitive, legal, regulatory, data-quality, compliance, liability, and reputational risks could materially harm the business.

Coherent Corp. depends on the experience and continuing services of certain scientists, engineers, production, sales, and management personnel and states that its success requires attracting, retaining, and developing key personnel while maintaining good employee relations. Intense competition could prevent Coherent from retaining or attracting necessary personnel, and loss of key personnel, inadequate succession planning, poor employee relations, or difficulty motivating key talent could materially adversely affect its business, results of operations, financial condition, and differentiated knowledge base.

Coherent Corp. states that close collaboration between its development and manufacturing teams improves project execution, reduces costs, accelerates technology transfers, and provides employee development opportunities; manufacturing personnel support or participate in R&D on an ongoing basis as of August 14, 2026.

Coherent does business with aerospace and defense customers that generally contract with governmental entities; Coherent states that its exposure to aerospace and defense demand is generally linked to government contracting. This current business statement contrasts with Coherent's separate disclosure that it divested its aerospace and defense business on September 2, 2025.

Coherent Corp. manufactures GaAs VCSELs and VCSEL arrays, InP edge-emitting lasers and photodiodes, and specialty glass wafers for consumer electronics. Its vertically integrated 6-inch GaAs platform supports high-volume, high-reliability applications including 3D sensing in smartphones, tablets, AR/VR headsets, smart watches, household robots, datacenters, HDMI optical cables, and automotive systems.

Sherri Luther has more than 30 years of strategic and financial operations experience, including financial reporting, forecasting, internal audit, M&A, treasury, investor relations, operations, and global supply chain management.

Coherent Corp. warns that increased competition and competitors' or customers' potential backward integration into Coherent's competencies could displace the company and adversely affect its business, market position, or customers' dependence on its products and capabilities; as of August 14, 2026, it stated that it may inaccurately estimate their willingness and capability to do so.

Coherent Corp. issued $990 million aggregate principal amount of 5.000% Senior Notes on December 10, 2021, due December 15, 2029. Interest is payable semiannually on June 15 and December 15 beginning June 15, 2022. The notes are guaranteed by Coherent’s domestic subsidiaries that guarantee its Senior Credit Facilities, with U.S. Bank National Association serving as trustee. As of June 30, 2026, the notes were part of Coherent’s approximately $3.2 billion of consolidated indebtedness and generated $51 million of interest expense during fiscal 2026, compared with $50 million during fiscal 2025.

Coherent Corp. contracts with large end-user service providers and product companies that have considerable bargaining power, creating a risk that Coherent must accept unfavorable or onerous terms covering pricing, warranties, indemnification, production capability, most-favored-customer rights, or exclusivity. These terms may delay revenue recognition, increase costs, restrict business with other customers, and create material liabilities if Coherent cannot satisfy contractual requirements. Large-customer concentration, cancellations, purchase reductions or delays, and disruptions in customers' sole-source supply chains could materially harm Coherent's revenue and business.

Noncontrolling interests in Silicon Carbide LLC decreased from $353.508 million at June 30, 2025 to $334.705 million at June 30, 2026, reflecting an $18.114 million net loss and $(0.689) million of foreign-currency translation adjustments during fiscal 2026.

Coherent Corp.'s intangible assets other than goodwill had a net book value of $2,884.474 million at June 30, 2026, compared with $3,204.747 million at June 30, 2025; customer lists and technology were the largest disclosed categories at $1,550.078 million and $904.396 million, respectively.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp.'s other accrued liabilities totaled $347.990 million, including $48.098 million of contract liabilities, a $27.454 million warranty reserve, $11.006 million of current liabilities held for sale, and $261.432 million of other accrued liabilities. A separate disclosure reported $10 million of liabilities for restructuring-related asset write-offs and other contract costs in other accrued liabilities and $12 million in other liabilities. The company also separately reported $7 million of severance-related costs in other accrued liabilities and $22 million in other liabilities, with cash expenditures expected through fiscal 2028; another disclosure reported $23 million of accrued severance-related costs in other accrued liabilities and expected expenditures primarily through fiscal 2027. The disclosures' reconciliation is not specified.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. had future minimum lease payments of $391.070 million, including $374.510 million for operating leases and $16.560 million for finance leases; the present value of total lease liabilities was $330.443 million. Separately, Coherent estimated approximately $375 million of operating lease obligations, including $78 million payable in fiscal year 2027.

Coherent Corp. recorded a sale of shares of noncontrolling interests that, net of $31.840 million of issuance costs and $127.389 million of taxes, increased common-stock amount by $464.327 million, noncontrolling interests by $373.573 million, and total shareholders' equity by $840.771 million.

Under Amendment No. 5 dated September 26, 2025, Coherent Corp.'s New Term B-2 Loans were replaced with an equal amount of New Term B-3 Loans; as of June 30, 2026, the New Term B-3 Loans bore interest at a SOFR-based rate subject to a 0.50% floor plus 1.75% and matured on July 1, 2029.
Coherent Corp.'s fiscal 2026 revenue was $7,118,181 ($000), compared with $5,810,115 ($000) in fiscal 2025 and $4,707,688 ($000) in fiscal 2024.

AI datacenter customers require access to clean water and predictable energy supplies; shortages or regulations limiting energy, water, or land availability could constrain their development and growth and negatively affect Coherent Corp.

Coherent Corp.'s supply-chain concentration in certain geographic regions leaves operations and profitability vulnerable to geopolitical tensions and military conflicts, including those in the Middle East and Ukraine, which could change regulatory requirements, disrupt supplies, restrict market access, or reduce product demand.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported fair values of $974,437 ($000) for its Senior Notes, $1,142,051 ($000) for its Term A Facility, and $1,082,030 ($000) for its Term B Facility, compared with carrying values of $986,057 ($000), $1,134,859 ($000), and $1,058,772 ($000), respectively. At June 30, 2025, the Senior Notes had a fair value of $973,190 ($000) and carrying value of $985,034 ($000), the Term A Facility had a fair value of $632,960 ($000) and carrying value of $616,234 ($000), and the Term B Facility had a fair value of $2,108,938 ($000) and carrying value of $2,065,880 ($000). Coherent classified the measurements as Level 2 and stated that limited trading volume means the estimates may not represent the values at which the debt could be retired or transferred.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp.'s outstanding performance share unit grants covered performance periods ranging from 12 to 36 months, with payment contingent on achieving specified levels of financial performance during those periods.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. reported net deferred income taxes of $(471,176) ($000), comprising deferred tax assets of $475,291 ($000) and deferred tax liabilities of $(946,467) ($000), compared with net deferred income taxes of $(658,310) ($000) as of June 30, 2025. The largest 2026 deferred tax liability was related to intangible assets at $(725,095) ($000).

Coherent Corp.'s unrecognized tax benefits decreased from $124,008 ($000) at June 30, 2025 to $63,759 ($000) at June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting a $67,049 ($000) reduction from expiration of statutes of limitations. At June 30, 2026, approximately $8 million of the remaining unrecognized tax benefit was expected to affect the effective tax rate, while Coherent expected an additional $3 million decrease during the following 12 months; most of the uncertain tax position liability could be offset by credit carryforwards and therefore would not impact cash taxes.

Coherent Corp.’s fiscal 2025 amortization expense included $17 million of impairment charges in the Industrial segment related to abandoning purchased technology and licenses; $14 million was recorded in cost of goods sold and $3 million in R&D, while fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2024 amortization expense included no impairment charges.

Coherent Corp. expenses internally developed technology costs as incurred, including allocated costs for wafer fabrication and other manufacturing facilities and resources used to support R&D programs.

Coherent Corp. reported that assets and liabilities held for sale were in its Industrial segment at both June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025. Current assets held for sale were $28,614 ($000) at June 30, 2026 versus $152,679 ($000) at June 30, 2025; noncurrent assets were $— versus $334,927 ($000); current liabilities were $11,006 ($000) versus $57,394 ($000); and noncurrent liabilities were $2,394 ($000) versus $28,635 ($000), respectively.

In connection with its acquisition of Coherent, Inc. on July 1, 2022, Coherent Corp. assumed all assets and liabilities of defined-benefit plans in the United States, Germany, South Korea, Japan, Spain, and Italy. The plans are generally unfunded, except that the Spanish plan and the U.S. qualified plan are partially funded.

Under ASC 606, Coherent Corp. measures revenue net of variable consideration, primarily estimated product returns and distributor sales price reductions arising from price-protection agreements, using historical analysis. Sales commissions are expensed when incurred because the amortization period would be one year or less and are recorded in SG&A.

As of June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. had an assumed acquisition-related Facility Construction Loan in Germany with $14 million of principal outstanding. The loan bears interest at 1.55% per annum, requires quarterly payments, and is due in 2030.

Coherent Corp.'s goodwill was $4,375,597 ($000) as of June 30, 2026, compared with $4,471,084 ($000) as of June 30, 2025. The fiscal 2026 change included $24,493 ($000) of other reclassifications, including adjustments to goodwill classified as held-for-sale, and a $(119,980) ($000) foreign-currency translation adjustment.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, Coherent Corp. obtained $135,996 ($000) of right-of-use assets in exchange for new operating lease liabilities, compared with $51,357 ($000) in 2025 and $64,385 ($000) in 2024.

Under Coherent Corp.’s supply chain financing program, participating suppliers may receive accelerated payment from third-party financial institutions while Coherent preserves its normal negotiated payment terms and accounts-payable classification; Coherent provides no guarantees, has no economic interest in suppliers’ participation, receives no economic benefit from the financial institutions, pledges no assets, and remains obligated to pay invoices in full. Supplier-accelerated accounts payable were $27 million as of June 30, 2026, compared with $18 million as of June 30, 2025; financial institutions paid $104 million of supplier invoices during fiscal 2026, compared with $76 million during fiscal 2025.
Ernst & Young LLP has served as Coherent Corp.'s auditor since 2008.

Coherent Corp. reported net cash provided by operating activities of $79,514 ($000) for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared with $633,600 ($000) in 2025 and $545,731 ($000) in 2024, indicating sharply lower operating cash generation in fiscal 2026; the company also reported net cash used in investing activities of $1,413,724 ($000) in 2026.

Ernst & Young LLP provided the independent registered public accounting firm's report on Coherent Corp.'s internal control over financial reporting for the annual report filed August 14, 2026; the report was included in Item 8 of the Form 10-K. Ernst & Young audited the controls under PCAOB standards and issued an unqualified opinion that they were effective as of June 30, 2026.
Coherent Corp. reported that the weighted average interest rate of total borrowings was 5% for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared with 6% for the year ended June 30, 2025.

Coherent Corp. reported total debt of $3,222,224 ($000) as of June 30, 2026, down from $3,686,921 ($000) as of June 30, 2025. The June 30, 2026 debt comprised a Term A Facility of $1,140,625 ($000) at adjusted SOFR plus 1.25%, a Term B Facility of $1,080,000 ($000) at adjusted SOFR plus 1.75%, 5.00% Senior Notes of $990,000 ($000), an Other Credit Facility of $28,004 ($000), local lines of credit of $4,791 ($000), and a facility construction loan in Germany of $14,062 ($000).
